answer: Mechanism: *sparse adjacency reaping*. Each agent holds a weighted `ledge` to one randomly assigned peer each epoch; only pairs mutually referencing each other at a shared `vertex` in the interaction graph retain their assigned weight, so an agent's survival depends on maintaining a live reciprocal link, not on accumulating clones. An attacker who mints many fake IDs must pay a per-identity cost of sustaining a distinct, active counterpart edge for every clone, because a `willow`-like mass of dangling unilateral links is pruned outright at the end of each epoch.
